article_content: NEW HAVEN, Connecticut (CNN) — A Yale University lab technician was arrested Thursday and charged with murder in the killing of graduate student Annie Le, whose body was found in the basement wall of an off-campus medical research building, police said. Raymond Clark, 24, was taken into custody and charged with murder. His bond was set at $3 million. Clark was apprehended at approximately 8:10 a.m. ET at a Super 8 motel in Cromwell, Connecticut, where he had stayed overnight after being released Wednesday following voluntary DNA testing. New Haven Police Chief James Lewis confirmed the bond amount. Hours after his arrest, Clark appeared in court but did not enter a plea. Standing with ankle restraints and hands on the table, he looked only at the judge and acknowledged that his rights had been read to him. A court date of October 6 has been scheduled. Lewis described the incident as an act of workplace violence but provided no further details. Annie Le’s body was discovered on Sunday in the basement wall of the research building. She had been strangled. The 24-year-old pharmacology student was last seen alive on September 8, when surveillance footage showed her entering a four-story lab at 10 Amistad Street, about 10 blocks from Yale’s main campus. Her body was found on what would have been her wedding day. Lewis said the arrest 'went smoothly' but declined to disclose specifics about the charges or whether DNA evidence directly led to the arrest, citing a sealed warrant. 'No further information can be released in order to comply with this court order,' he said. Clark could have been arrested Wednesday had he refused to provide DNA samples or permit a search of his residence, but he was released after cooperating, according to New Haven city spokeswoman Jessica Mayorga. Police had been monitoring the motel where Clark was staying. When questioned about the arrest, Clark’s attorney, David Dworski, referred CNN to a previous statement: 'We are committed to proceeding appropriately with the authorities with whom we are in regular contact.' Two additional search warrants were executed Wednesday: one targeting property not included in the initial warrant, and another for Clark’s vehicle, which was being processed Wednesday evening. Lewis described Clark as a technician performing custodial duties in the building. He answered initial police questions but later invoked his right to counsel and ceased speaking. Yale President Richard Levin said the administration is 'relieved' by the arrest but urged the community to 'resist the temptation to rush to judgment.' Clark, employed at Yale since December 2004, had no prior indicators in his employment history suggesting involvement in such a crime, Levin added. Lewis stated that Clark and Le worked in the same building and occasionally crossed paths in hallways but refused to confirm whether they knew each other personally. Investigators have collected approximately 250 pieces of evidence. More than 700 hours of video footage have been reviewed, and over 150 individuals have been interviewed — some multiple times. Although authorities have not disclosed specific DNA findings, they previously revealed that bloody clothing was discovered hidden above ceiling tiles in another section of the building. However, Thomas Kaplan, editor-in-chief of the Yale Daily News, reported that a Yale police official confirmed the garments were not what Le was wearing when she entered the building. Teams from the Connecticut State Police lab processed the bloodstained clothing over the weekend. Police have not described the items or identified their owner. Lewis noted that processing of the building was nearing completion and expected to be cleared by Thursday morning. Le was scheduled to marry Jonathan Widawsky, a Columbia University graduate student, on Sunday on Long Island, New York. Originally from Placerville, California, Le had shown awareness of campus safety concerns. In February, she wrote an article for B magazine comparing safety measures across Ivy League schools, advising students to carry minimal personal items. On the day she disappeared, she left her purse, credit cards, and cellphone in her office.
translated_content: NEW HAVEN, Konektikat (CNN) — Tehničar sa Yale univerziteta hapšen je u četvrtak i optužen za ubistvo diplomirane studentice Ani Le, čiji je trup pronađen u zidu podzemlja vankampusne medicinske istraživačke zgrade, rekli su policajci. Raymond Clark, 24, uhvaćen je i optužen za ubistvo. Njegova naknada je postavljena na 3 miliona dolara. Clark je uhvaćen oko 8:10 jutarnjeg vremena po istočnom vremenu u motelu Super 8 u Cromwellu, Konektikat, gdje je proveo noć nakon što je pušten u srijedu nakon dobijanja uzoraka DNK. Policijski šef iz Nju Havena, Džejms Luiš, potvrdio je iznos naknade. Sat vremena nakon hapšenja, Clark se pojavio pred sudom, ali nije dao odgovor. Stajao je sa ograničenjima na gležnjima i rukama na stolu, gledao je samo sudiju i potvrdio da su mu pročitana njegova prava. Datum sudskog procesa postavljen je na 6. oktobar. Luiš je opisao slučaj kao akt nasilja na radnom mjestu, ali nije dao dodatne detalje. Trup Ani Le pronađen je u nedelju u zidu podzemlja istraživačke zgrade. Bila je gušena. 24-godišnja studentica farmakologije posljednji put je viđena živa 8. septembra, kada je snimka nadzora pokazala kako ulazi u četvoronivou zgradu na 10 Amistad Street, otprilike deset blokova od glavnog kampusa. Njen trup je pronađen onoga dana kada bi trebalo da se uda. Luiš je rekao da je hapšenje 'prošlo glatko', ali se odrekao objavljivanja detalja o optužbama ili da li su rezultati DNK doveli do hapšenja Klarka, navodeći zaključeni nalaz. 'Nijedan dodatni podatak ne može biti objavljen kako bi se poštovao ovaj sudski nalog,' rekao je. Clark bi mogao biti hapšen u srijedu da je odbio da pruži uzorke DNK ili da dopusti pretragu svog doma, ali je pušten nakon saradnje, prema poručnici grada Nju Havena, Džesiki Majorgi. Policija je pratila motel u kojem je Clark boravio. Kad su ga pitali o hapšenju, Clarkov advokat, Devid Dvorski, uputio je CNN na ranije objavljeni izjavu: 'Zalagamo se da postupamo odgovorno sa autoritetima sa kojima smo u redovnoj komunikaciji.' U srijedu su izvršena još dva nalaza za pretragu: jedan na imovini koja nije bila uključena u prvobitni nalaz, i drugi za Clarkov vozilo, koje je obrađivano večer u srijedu. Luiš je opisao Klarka kao tehničara koji obavlja poslove poput održavanja u zgradi. Odgovorio je na nekoliko pitanja policije, ali kasnije je pozvao advokata i prestao da priča. Predsjednik Yalea, Ričard Levin, rekao je da je administracija 'olakšana' zbog hapšenja, ali da poziva zajednicu da 'otpori iskušenju da brzo donese sudove'. Clark, zapošlen na Yaleu od decembra 2004. godine, nije imao nikakve prethodne indikacije u svojoj radnoj historiji koje bi ukazivale na mogućnost uključenosti u takav zločin, dodao je Levin. Luiš je naveo da su Clark i Le radile u istoj zgradi i povremeno se susrećale u hodnicima, ali je odbio da potvrdi da li su se poznali lično. Istraživači su sakupili otprilike 250 komada dokaza. Pregledano je više od 700 sati snimaka, a više od 150 ljudi je intervjuisano — neki više puta. Iako vlasti nisu objavile specifične DNK nalaze, ranije su otkrile da su krvave odeće pronađene skrivene iznad ploča u plafonu u drugom dijelu zgrade. Međutim, Tomas Kaplan, urednik glasnika Yale Daily News, rekao je da je predstavnik Yale police rekao novinarima da te odeće nisu bile one koje je Le nosila kad je ušla u zgradu. Timovi sa laboratorije policijske uprave Konektikata obrađivali su krvave odeće tokom vikenda. Policija nije opisala te predmete ni identifikovala njihovog vlasnika. Luiš je napomenuo da je obrada zgrade blizu završetka i da se očekuje da će biti oslobođena u četvrtak jutrom. Le je trebala da se uda u nedelju na Long Ajlandu, Nju Jork, sa Jonatanom Vidavskim, diplomiranim studentom Univerziteta Kolumbija. Rođena u Plaservilu, Kalifornija, Le je pokazala svijest o sigurnosnim problemima na fakultetu. U februaru je napisala članak za časopis B u kojem je poređila mjere sigurnosti među Ivy League školama, savjetujući studente da nose minimalno osobnih stvari. Dana kad je nestala, ostavila je svoj torbu, kreditne kartice i mobilni telefon u svom kancelarijskom prostoru.

article_content: During a planned nature hike near Torrey Pines State Beach, a group of young Cub Scouts from Troop 766 accidentally wandered onto Black’s Beach — a well-known clothing-optional stretch of coastline. The boys, mostly nine and ten years old, were surprised to encounter dozens of adults enjoying the beach without swimwear. The scout leader, familiar with the area and unaware of how others might view it, assumed the path was a regular trail. Parents reacted strongly upon learning what had occurred. One mother, Diane Lekven, described feeling sickened by the sight of strangers nude and holding hands, calling the experience deeply unsettling for her child. While the Boy Scouts Association confirmed the group was immediately redirected once the situation was noticed, some families questioned whether the route choice was truly accidental. Officials from the San Diego-Imperial Council later held meetings with parents to review the incident. They concluded that safety protocols were followed and no further disciplinary action was necessary. Black’s Beach, publicly designated by the Naturist Society as a clothing-optional area, has long been permitted under local regulations.

Dječaci, većinom devet i deset godina starosti, bili su iznenađeni kada su susreli desetine odraslih koji su uživali na plaži bez odjeće. Vođa skauta, koji je bio upoznat s tim područjem i nesvjestan kako bi drugi to shvatili, pretpostavio je da je staza obična. Roditelji su jako reagirali kad su saznali što se dogodilo. Jedna majka, Diane Lekven, rekla je da joj je bilo neugodno gledati strance golih i držeći se za ruke, nazivajući iskustvo duboko neprikladnim za njezinu djecu. Iako je Asocijacija skauta potvrdila da je grupa odmah preusmjerena čim je situacija uočena, neki roditelji su se pitali je li izbor staze bio zaista slučajan. Službenici iz San Diego-Imperial savjeta kasnije su održali sastanke s roditeljima kako bi pregledali incident. Zaključili su da su protokoli sigurnosti pridržani i da nije bilo potrebno dodatno djelovanje. Black’s Beach, javno označen od strane Naturističkog društva kao područje s opcionalnom odjećom, dugo je bio dopušten prema lokalnim zakonima.

article_content: For years, Ronald McDonald seemed to vanish from public view—sparking wild rumors, including one that he shanked Grimace in a Mexican alley. Whether true or not, the clown is back—and McDonald’s is making sure everyone knows it. On Wednesday, the company announced Ronald’s global mission: to inspire joy through community events. While we’d love to see him on a motorcycle with AC/DC blasting, the reality is likely less explosive. Still, it’s good to see him working again. Let’s be honest: finding stable employment when your resume includes ‘professional clown’ and ‘expert in tearful bedtime routines’ isn’t easy. But Ronald isn’t just a smiling face in makeup. Behind the greasepaint lies a relentless corporate force—a hamburger kingpin who barks, 'Put that McCafe coffee down! McCafe’s for closers only.' Critics say he encourages kids to eat unhealthy food. And yes, the formula is simple: 'Hey kids, look at the funny clown! Want a Happy Meal?' But let’s not pretend McDonald’s is a tattoo parlor. 'Hey kids, look at the funny clown! Want a koi fish on your neck?' He sells burgers. That’s it. Still, even legends evolve. As societal norms shift, so must icons. That’s why Ronald’s new wardrobe was designed by Ann Hould-Ward, Tony Award-winning costume designer known for her work on Broadway’s 'Beauty and the Beast'—and for creating promotional costumes for McDonald’s live appearances. His new look? Cargo pants, a technical vest, and a classic red-and-white striped rugby shirt—basically, Old Navy essentials. Surprisingly, it works. He looks like a laid-back 20-something headed to a Dave Matthews concert. And thankfully, his giant red shoes remain untouched. He also now owns a whimsical new blazer—for special occasions, like a bris. 'Nice work, Rabbi.' 'Thanks, Clown.' Beyond fashion, McDonald’s unveiled a new mantra: 'Fun makes great things happen.' The idea? Joy sparks kindness. Maybe it’s true—I once left my house without pants and ended up volunteering at a bake sale. Who knew? Most exciting? Ronald now has access to McDonald’s official Twitter account. No personal handle—but he can be referenced via the hashtag #RonaldMcDonald. Yes, the same guy who hangs out with The Hamburglar. The trust is... bold. And while he’s unlikely to post drunk selfies after a Tinder date, the hashtag is already trending. 'Boom! Two words. BIG MAC. #RonaldMcDonald #Legendary.' At its core, this is just corporate branding dressed up as nostalgia. But if a clown in cargo pants can make someone smile—even for a second—maybe that’s enough.

Da li je istina ili ne, joker se vratio — i McDonald’s je osigurao da svi znaju. U srijedu je kompanija objavila Ronaldovu globalnu misiju: da inspiriše radost kroz zajedničke događaje. Dok bismo voljeli da ga vidimo na motociklu sa AC/DC-om koji puca iz zvučnika, stvarnost je vjerojatno manje eksplozivna. Ipak, dobro je što radi ponovo. Priznajmo: pronaći stabilan posao kad vaš životopis uključuje 'profesionalni joker' i 'stručnjak za suze pri spavanju' nije lako. Ali Ronald nije samo osmijeh u farbi. Iza te farbe leži nesavladiv korporativni silovac — kralj hamburghera koji vrišti: 'Spusti taj McCafe kafu! McCafe je samo za one koji završe prodaju!' Kritičari kažu da potiče djecu da jede nezdravu hranu. I da, formula je jednostavna: 'Hej, djeco, pogledajte smiješnog jokera! Želite li Happy Meal?' Ali ne pretpostavljajmo da je McDonald’s tetovažni saloon. 'Hej, djeco, pogledajte smiješnog jokera! Želite li koi ribicu na vratu?' On prodaje hamburgere. To je sve. Ipak, čak i legende moraju da se razvijaju. Kako se društveni normi mijenjaju, tako moraju i ikone. Zato je Ronaldov novi garderobu dizajnirala Ann Hould-Ward, dobitnica Tony nagrade za svoj rad na Broadway-ovoj predstavi 'Lijepa i zvijer', i koja je dizajnirala reklamne kostime za McDonaldsove žive nastupe. Njegov novi izgled? Radne hlače, tehnička jakna i klasična crveno-bijela prugasta rugby košulja — u osnovi, osnovne stvari iz Old Navy. Iznenadujuće, radi. Izgleda kao opušteni dvadesetogodišnjak koji ide na koncert Dave Matthews Band-a. I srećom, njegove ogromne crvene cipele ostaju netaknute. Također ima novi, šaljiv jaknu — za posebne prilike, poput brisa. 'Dobar rad, rabine.' 'Hvala, jokeru.' Osim odeće, McDonald’s je objavio novi moto: 'Radoznalost stvara velike stvari.' Ideja? Radost pokreće dobrotu. Možda je istina — jednom sam izašao iz kuće bez hlača i završio sam kao volonter na prodaji kolača. Tko bi znao? Najuzbuđujuće? Ronald ima pristup službenom Twitter računu McDonald’sa. Nema osobni profil — ali može biti spominjan putem hashtaga #RonaldMcDonald. Da, isti tip koji se druži s Hamburglarom. Povjerenje je... smiješno. I dok je vjerojatno nemoguće da objavljuje slike nakon Tinder datuma, hashtag već trendira. 'Boom! Dva riječi. BIG MAC. #RonaldMcDonald #Legenda.' Na kraju krajeva, ovo je samo korporativno branding obučeno kao nostalgija. Ali ako joker u radnim hlačama može natjerati nekoga da osmijehne — čak i na trenutak — možda je to dovoljno.

article_content: Surgeons at Johns Hopkins Hospital have released images capturing the historic moment when U.S. Army Sergeant Brendan Marrocco, a quadruple amputee injured in a 2009 roadside bomb blast in Iraq, underwent a double-arm transplant. Marrocco, a 26-year-old from Staten Island, New York, said he is eager to regain independence—particularly to drive his black Dodge Charger and swim again. 'I just want to get the most out of these arms,' he said at a press conference. 'As goals come up, I’ll knock them down and take it as far as I can.' The 13-hour surgery, performed on December 18, 2012, was the first bilateral arm transplant at Johns Hopkins and only the seventh such procedure in the United States. In addition to the transplanted limbs, Marrocco received bone marrow from the same donor—a novel approach designed to reduce lifelong immunosuppressive medication and lower long-term cancer risks. Dr. Jaimie Shores, clinical director of hand transplantation at Hopkins, praised Marrocco’s optimism and determination. 'He's a young man with tremendous hope—and stubborn in a good way,' Shores said. 'I think the sky's the limit.' Although Marrocco currently lacks sensation in his fingers, he has already begun attempting to move his hands. Nerve regeneration occurs at approximately one inch per month, meaning full functional recovery could take two to three years. Marrocco is the first soldier to survive losing all four limbs in the Iraq War. He will continue intensive rehabilitation at Johns Hopkins for two years, followed by care at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center. His father, Alex Marrocco, expressed deep gratitude to the donor’s family: 'They made a selfless decision that made a profound difference in Brendan’s life.' Unlike life-saving organ transplants, limb transplants focus exclusively on restoring quality of life. Prosthetic arms remain technologically limited compared to leg prosthetics, making such surgeries vital for amputees seeking autonomy. Dr. W.P. Andrew Lee, who led the surgery and pioneered the bone marrow infusion technique at the University of Pittsburgh, called Marrocco’s case 'the most complicated' of his career. Five previous patients treated similarly have succeeded with reduced drug regimens. Marrocco, who had been living in a specially adapted home on Staten Island—later damaged by Superstorm Sandy—said he has no regrets about his military service. 'I wouldn’t change it in any way. I’m still the same person.' Despite enduring significant postoperative pain, Marrocco lightened the mood by joking that his hoarse voice from intubation sounded like Al Pacino—and began reciting movie lines to make nurses laugh.

'On je mladi čovjek sa ogromnom nadom—i uporan na dobar način,' rekao je Shores. 'Mislim da su granice neograničene.' Regeneracija živaca događa se brzinom otprilike jedan centimetar mjesečno, što znači da bi puna funkcionalna oporavka mogla trajati dva do tri godine. On će nastaviti intenzivnu rehabilitaciju na Johns Hopkinsu tijekom dvije godine, nakon čega će biti prebačen na Walter Reed Nacionalni vojni medicinski centar. Andrew Lee, koji je vodio operaciju i osmislio tehniku transfuzije koštane srži na Sveučilištu Pittsburgh, nazvao je Marroccov slučaj 'najkomplikovanijim' u svom poslu. I dalje sam ista osoba.' Iako je trpio značajnu postoperativnu bol, Marrocco je olakšao raspoloženje šaljom da mu je hrapav glas od intubacije podsjeća na Al Pacina—i počeo je recitirati filmove da bi naterao medicinsko osoblje da se nasmije.

article_content: By Mark Prigg. PUBLISHED: 09:47 EST, 5 November 2012. | UPDATED: 10:53 EST, 5 November 2012. While it didn’t attract the massive queues of previous launches, Apple revealed that sales of its new iPad mini were anything but small. The company announced it sold three million iPads — including the new iPad mini and fourth-generation iPad — in just three days since launch. This figure doubles the previous record of 1.5 million Wi-Fi-only units sold during the third-generation iPad’s launch in March. The iPad mini went on sale globally on Friday. Although it failed to draw long lines outside stores, Apple reported selling three million new iPads within 72 hours. Many online pre-orders sold out within hours, though retail stores maintained sufficient stock on launch day. However, new data from IDC shows Apple’s share of the global tablet market has fallen from two-thirds to just over half in the past six months, as Google’s Android platform gains popularity. IDC reported that Apple’s third-quarter worldwide tablet shipment share dropped from 59.7% a year earlier to 50.4% by the end of September. Meanwhile, Samsung’s share surged from 6.5% to 18.4%. Amazon captured 9% of the market with its Kindle Fire devices, while Asus — which manufactures Google’s Nexus 7 — increased its global share from 3.8% to 8.6%. Apple held 65.5% of the market in the second quarter. Both the iPad mini and the new fourth-generation iPad with Retina display are available in 34 countries, including the U.S., Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, and the UK. More countries, including mainland China, will receive them later this year. Demand for the iPad mini exceeded initial supply. While most pre-orders have shipped, some remain scheduled for delivery later this month. Apple’s Phil Schiller unveiled the iPad mini at a special event in California, stating: 'You can hold it in one hand. This isn’t a shrunken-down iPad — it’s an entirely new design.' 'The iPad mini is as thin as a pencil and as light as a pad of paper, yet packs a fast A5 chip, FaceTime HD, a 5-megapixel iSight camera, and ultrafast wireless connectivity — all while delivering up to 10 hours of battery life,' Schiller added. The device will compete directly with Amazon’s $199 Kindle Fire and Google’s $159 Nexus 7, prompting experts to predict a 'tablet bloodbath.' It also faces competition from Microsoft’s larger 10.6-inch Surface tablet, priced at $399. Wi-Fi + Cellular versions of both iPads will begin shipping in the U.S. in a few weeks, followed by additional countries later this year.

article_content: In the UK, your eyebrows might reveal more about where you’re from than your accent does. New observations suggest that regional eyebrow trends have become so distinct, people can guess a woman’s hometown just by looking at her brows — often before she speaks. In southern England, from London to Brighton, women are embracing the ‘South brow’: full, lush, and naturally tinted, inspired by stars like the Duchess of Cambridge, Keira Knightley, and Cara Delevingne. Unlike the harsh, dark lines of the North, this style leans into soft volume and subtlety — think ‘effortlessly groomed,’ not ‘dramatic stage makeup.’ Meanwhile, up north in Liverpool, Manchester, and Leeds, the ‘Scouse brow’ reigns supreme — thick, sharply angled, and deeply filled in, popularized by figures like Coleen Rooney and Alex Gerrard. Shoppers in these areas buy nearly twice as many dark eyebrow pencils and waxes compared to the South. In Wales, the preferred look is a gentle, elegant arch — a signature of Catherine Zeta-Jones — while Irish women tend toward the ‘tadpole brow’: thick and rounded at the inner edge, tapering sharply into a fine tail. Interestingly, Ireland reports the lowest sales of eyebrow products nationally. Further west, women in Birmingham and Coventry favor the ‘happy brow’ — a softly curved, rounded shape that looks perpetually cheerful. In Scotland, the ‘plank brow’ dominates: straight, unbroken, and minimalistic, worn by DJs like Edith Bowman. Beauty experts at Debenhams note a cultural pivot: gone are the days of razor-thin brows. Today, eyebrows are bold, intentional, and proudly regional — a quiet form of identity politics written in pigment and hair. As one beauty director puts it: 'It’s like a brow-o-meter. You see it, you know where they’re from.'

article_content: In the quiet streets of Detroit’s Grandmont neighborhood, a modest three-bedroom home sits quietly — its walls still holding the echoes of past lives, its future now reshaped by a new kind of American dream. Bought for just $12,000 in March, this house, worth an estimated $110,000, was flipped within days for $17,000. Its buyer? Jeremy Burgess, a former Washington state baker turned Detroit real estate entrepreneur. Alongside partner Jared Pomranky, Burgess runs Urban Detroit Wholesalers, a company that buys, fixes, and resells homes in a city many have written off. But Burgess sees something different: a market frozen in time, where land is dirt cheap, and opportunity is wide open. 'Detroit is the new Wild West,' he says. 'You can’t find affordable land out west anymore — it’s here now.' Across the city, abandoned homes line streets, some listed for as little as a dollar. But beneath the shocking price tags lies a harsh truth: most of these houses need tens of thousands in repairs, and banks or desperate owners simply want to escape the burden of taxes and liability. Tearing them down costs more than the land is worth, so giving them away becomes the only rational choice. Of the last 800 sales in the area, only about 10 went to actual residents looking to live there — the rest were bought by investors, mostly from California and other states, seeking alternatives to volatile stock markets. Yet, not all of Detroit is crumbling. On its northwestern and northeastern edges, sturdy middle-class neighborhoods remain intact, with homes holding steady value. These are the areas Burgess and Pomranky target — not the ruins, but the resilient blocks where families still want to live. Renovated homes typically sell for around $35,000, with 60% becoming rentals and 40% finding new owners. Crucially, nearly every dollar spent stays in Detroit. Workers hired are locals — many are formerly incarcerated men and women rebuilding their lives. Materials come from Detroit hardware stores. Paychecks are deposited in Detroit bank accounts. For Burgess, this isn’t just a business — it’s a lifeline. He remembers arriving in the city in 2007 with $35,000 and a handful of properties — only to watch the housing crash wipe him out. He almost quit. Then he met Pomranky. Together, they rebuilt their model around partnerships with nonprofits like Motor City Blight Busters, which provides affordable labor and helps place families in restored homes. 'We’re not just flipping houses,' says John George, president of the nonprofit. 'We’re restoring dignity, one home at a time.' While the scale is small — about 100 homes per year — the impact is profound. And Burgess believes this model could work anywhere: when private enterprise and community action align, even the most broken systems can begin to heal.

Kupljen za samo 12.000 dolara u martu, ovaj dom, koji se procjenjuje na oko 110.000 dolara, prodan je unutar dana za 17.000 dolara. Njegov kupac? Jeremy Burgess, bivši pekar iz Washingtona koji je postao poduzetnik u domaćinstvu u Detroitu. U partnerstvu sa Jaredom Pomrankyjem, Burgess vodi Urban Detroit Wholesalers, tvrtku koja kupuje, popravlja i prodaje kuće u gradu koji su mnogi odbacili. Ali Burgess vidi nešto drugo: tržište koje je u stajanju, gdje je zemlja vrlo jeftina, a prilike široke. 'Detroit je novi Divlji zapad,' kaže on. 'Više ne možete pronaći jeftinu zemlju na Zapadu — sada je ovdje.' Po cijelom gradu, napuštene kuće redaju ulice, neke navedene za samo jedan dolar. Ali ispod šokantnih cijena leži kruta istina: većina ovih kuća zahtijeva desetke tisuća dolara za popravak, a banke ili očajni vlasnici jednostavno žele pobjeći od tereta poreza i odgovornosti. Rušenje kuća košta više nego što vrijedi zemlja, pa je davanje kuća besplatno jedina racionalna opcija. Od posljednjih 800 prodaja u području, samo je otprilike 10 otišlo stvarnim stanovnicima koji traže mjesto za život — ostatak su kupili investitori, uglavnom iz Kalifornije i drugih država, koji traže alternative nestabilnim tržištima akcija. Međutim, ne sve u Detroitu ruši se. Na njegovim sjeverozapadnim i sjeveroistočnim rubovima, čvrsti srednje klase kvartovi ostaju netaknuti, a kuće održavaju stabilnu vrijednost. To su područja koja Burgess i Pomranky ciljaju — ne ruševine, već otporne četvrti gdje porodice još uvijek žele živjeti. Popravljene kuće obično se prodaju za oko 35.000 dolara, pri čemu 60% postaje najam, a 40% nalazi nove vlasnike. Ključno je da gotovo svaki dolar trošen ostaje u Detroitu. Zaposleni su lokalci — mnogi su bivši zatvorenici koji obnavljaju svoje živote. Materijali dolaze iz detsroitskih trgovina alatima. Plaća se uplaćuju na detsroitske banke. Za Burgessa ovo nije samo posao — to je životna linija. Sjeća se kako je stigao u grad 2007. godine s 35.000 dolara i nekoliko svojstava — samo da bi gledao kako kreditni pad uništava sve. Skoro je odustao. Onda je upoznao Pomrankyja. Zajedno su ponovno izgradili svoj model oko suradnje s neprofitnim organizacijama poput Motor City Blight Busters, koje nude jeftin rad i pomažu smještiti porodice u obnovljene kuće. 'Ne samo da mijenjamo kuće,' kaže John George, predsjednik neprofitne organizacije. 'Obnavljamo dostojanstvo, jednu kuću odjednom.' Iako je razmjernost mala — oko 100 kuća godišnje — utjecaj je dubok. I Burgess vjeruje da ovaj model može raditi bilo gdje: kad privatno poduzeće i zajednička akcija budu u skladu, čak i najslabiji sustavi mogu početi liječiti.

article_content: In a green field just outside Peshawar, in northwestern Pakistan, the face of a young girl gazes upward, her eyes searching the sky for the drones that took her family. Her innocent expression, captured in a haunting photograph, now appears on a massive poster — part of #NotABugSplat, an art initiative by Pakistani artist-activists aiming to restore humanity to those killed by U.S. drone strikes in the country’s tribal regions. One artist, who goes by the initials R, explains that the project responds to the cold, detached language of drone warfare — terms like 'bug splat,' used to describe victims seen only as blurry figures on screens. 'Viewing a dead body through a grainy video feed makes it feel like crushing an insect,' he says. 'We want to shame the operators and force them to see the real human cost.' Inspired by French photographer JR’s global 'Inside Out' project, the team behind #NotABugSplat reached out to Reprive, a UK-based legal charity working with Pakistani lawyer Shehzad Akbar. Akbar provided them with a photo taken by North Waziristan-based photojournalist Noor Behram — an image of a girl whose parents were killed in a 2010 drone strike in the village of Dande Darpa Khel. That strike destroyed several mud-brick homes sheltering Afghan refugees. Most victims were women and children. The girl’s identity and exact whereabouts remain unknown, swallowed by the tide of displacement that defines this war-torn region. To ensure the poster would endure beyond its physical presence, the artists placed it in the field long enough to be captured by satellite imagery — embedding her face permanently into digital mapping platforms like Google Earth. Originally, they hoped to display it in Waziristan, the epicenter of drone activity. But due to military restrictions, they settled for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa instead. Though no drone strikes have been officially confirmed in Pakistan since December 2013, #NotABugSplat continues to create and display more portraits of children. 'Only the loss of a child can truly show the impact of these strikes,' says R. Drone strikes in Pakistan’s border regions have sparked widespread anger due to civilian deaths and eroded trust between Pakistan and the United States — tensions worsened by the 2011 U.S. raid that killed Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad. According to The Bureau of Investigative Journalism, over 380 U.S. drone strikes have occurred in Pakistan since 2004, with civilian death estimates ranging from 2,296 to 3,718.
translated_content: Na zelenom polju izvan Pešavara, u sjeverozapadnom Pakistanu, lice mlade djevojčice gleda prema nebu, njeni oči traže strojeve koji su ubili njenu obitelj. Njezino nevin izražavanje, uhvaćeno u žalosnoj fotografiji, sada se pojavljuje na ogromnom plakatu — dijelu projekta #NotABugSplat, umjetničke inicijative pakistanskih umjetnika-aktivista koja ima za cilj vratiti čovječnost onima koji su ubijeni američkim dronovima u tribalnim regijama zemlje. Jedan umjetnik, koji se koristi inicijalima R, objašnjava da je ovaj projekt odgovor na hladan, odvojen jezik ratovanja dronovima — izrazi poput 'bug splat', koji se koriste za opisivanje žrtava koje se vide samo kao mutne slike na ekranima. 'Gledanje mrtvog tijela kroz mutnu video sliku čini da se osjeća kao da se pritisne komarac,' kaže on. 'Želimo sramotiti operatore i natjerati ih da vide pravi ljudski trošak.' Inspriran globalnim projektom francuskog fotograf JR-a 'Inside Out', tim iza #NotABugSplat kontaktirao je Reprive, britansku pravnu dobrotvornu organizaciju koja radi s pakistanskim pravnikom Shehzadom Akbrom. Akbar im je dao fotografiju snimljenu od strane novinara iz sjevernog Waziristana, Noora Behrama — sliku djevojčice čiji su roditelji ubijeni u napadu dronom 2010. godine u selu Dande Darpa Khel. Taj napad uništio je nekoliko kuća od lijepe gline u kojima su smješteni afghanski izbjeglice. Većina žrtava bile su žene i djeca. Identitet djevojčice i njezino točno mjesto ostaju nepoznati, progutani valom raseljavanja koje definira ovaj ratom razoren područje. Da bi plakat ostao prisutan nakon fizičkog uklanjanja, umjetnici su ga postavili na polje dovoljno dugo da bude uhvaćen satelitskom slikom — trajno ugrađujući njeno lice u digitalne kartografske platforme poput Google Zemlje. Izvorno su htjeli prikazati ga u Waziristanu, središtu aktivnosti dronova. Ali zbog vojnih ograničenja, odabrali su provinciju Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Iako nijedan napad dronom nije potvrđen u Pakistanu od prosinca 2013., #NotABugSplat nastavlja stvarati i prikazivati više portreta djece. 'Samo gubitak djeteta može pravilno pokazati utjecaj ovih napada,' kaže R. Napadi dronovima u granicnim regijama Pakistana izazvali su široki gnjev zbog civilnih žrtava i oštetili povjerenje između Pakistana i SAD-a — napetosti koje su se pogoršale nakon američkog napada 2011. godine koji je ubio Osamu bin Ladena u Abbottabadu. Prema Biuro istraživačkih novinarstva, od 2004. godine u Pakistanu je izvršeno preko 380 američkih napada dronovima, a procijenjeni broj civilnih žrtava kreće se između 2.296 i 3.718.

article_content: More than half of Americans say the U.S. government should do a great deal or quite a bit to address the problem of climate change, according to a new Associated Press-GfK poll. A growing majority of Americans believe global warming is occurring, that it will become a serious problem, and that the U.S. government should take action—findings supported by the poll. Even most people who say they don’t trust scientists on environmental issues report observing rising temperatures. The poll found that 80% of Americans believe climate change will be a serious problem for the United States if nothing is done—up from 73% in 2009. Fifty-seven percent of respondents said the government should do a great deal or quite a bit to combat climate change, an increase from 52% in 2009. Only 22% believe little or nothing should be done, down from 25%. Overall, 78% of those surveyed believe temperatures have been rising—up from 75% three years earlier. Among those who trust scientists only a little or not at all, 61% now say temperatures have risen over the past century, a significant jump from 47% in 2009. Scientists view Greenland’s melting ice caps and disappearing glaciers as clear indicators of global warming. Jon Krosnick, a Stanford University social psychologist who helped design the poll, noted that shifts are not occurring among hard-core deniers but among those with lingering doubts: 'They don’t believe what scientists say—they believe what their thermometers say.' Phil Adams, a retired photographer from North Carolina, said he once doubted scientists but now sees clear evidence of warming through personal experience: 'The seasons are more severe. The climate is definitely getting warmer.' Nearly half—49%—described global warming as 'very serious,' up from 42% in 2009. While 57% want strong government action, only 45% believe President Barack Obama will take major steps in his second term, compared to 41% who think he won’t. Belief in rising temperatures peaked at 85% in 2006 following Hurricane Katrina and dipped to a 15-year low in late 2009 amid snowy winters and the 'Climategate' controversy—a scandal later debunked by independent investigations. By party, 83% of Democrats, 70% of Republicans, and 77% of independents agree the world is warming. According to a 2010 scientific review, 97% of publishing climate scientists endorse human-caused global warming. About one-quarter of respondents still worry that climate policies could harm the economy—down slightly from 27% in 2009. Forty-six percent believe such actions would help the economy, roughly unchanged from three years prior. The AP-GfK poll was conducted November 29 to December 3, 2012, via landline and cell phone interviews with 1,002 U.S. adults. Results carry a margin of error of ±3.9 percentage points. Anthony Leiserowitz of Yale’s Project on Climate Change Communication noted that economic stress and extreme snowfall in 2009 dampened belief, but recent persistent extreme weather has rekindled public connection to climate change: 'One extreme event after another... People are connecting the dots themselves.' Thomas Coffey, 77, of Houston, observed: 'We used to have mild fall temperatures leading into winter. Now, we have summer heat extending into winter. The Earth is getting warmer—and that’s why ice melts and oceans rise.' He linked this to disasters like Superstorm Sandy: 'Look at how long those flooded tunnels have been closed.' Visual evidence from Greenland—including melting icebergs in Jacobshavn Bay—reinforces these observations.

Rastuća većina Amerikanaca vjeruje da se globalno zagrijavanje događa, da će postati ozbiljan problem i da američka vlada treba poduzeti neke mjere – ovo potvrđuje istraživanje. Klima se sigurno zagrijava.' Skoro polovica – 49% – opisala je globalno zagrijavanje kao 'vrlo ozbiljno', rast s 42% u 2009. godini. Iako 57% želi jaču vladenu akciju, samo 45% vjeruje da će predsjednik Barack Obama poduzeti važne korake u njegovom drugom mandatu, u usporedbi s 41% koji misle da neće. Vjerovanje u porast temperatura dostiglo je vrhunac od 85% 2006. godine nakon uragana Katrina, a spalo na najnižu razinu u posljednjih 15 godina krajem 2009. godine tijekom snježnih zima i skandala 'Climategate' – incident kasnije odbačen neovisnim istraživanjima. Po strancima, 83% demokrata, 70% republikanaca i 77% neovisnih slaže se da se svijet zagrijava. Prema znanstvenom pregledu iz 2010. godine, 97% znanstvenika koji objavljuju radove o ovom temu podržava ljudsko uzrokovano globalno zagrijavanje. Oko jedne četvrtine ispitanika još uvijek brine da bi politike za smanjenje zagrijavanja mogle štetiti ekonomiji – lagani pad s 27% u 2009. godini. 46% misli da bi takve mjere pomoću američkoj ekonomiji, otprilike isto kao i prije tri godine. Istraživanje AP-GfK provedeno je od 29. studenoga do 3. prosinca 2012. godine putem poziva s fiksnih i mobitela s 1.002 odrasla osoba u cijelom SAD-u. Ljudi sami povezuju točke.' Tomás Kofei, 77-godišnjak iz Houstona, primjetio je: 'Rano smo imali blage temperature jeseni koja se spuštala u zimski period. Sada imamo ljetne temperature koje se protežu u zimu. Zemlja se zagrijava – i zato se led topi i mora raste.' On je povezao to s katastrofama poput Superuragana Sandy: 'Pogledajte koliko su dugo zatvoreni ti poplavljene tuneli.' Vizualni dokazi iz Grenlanda – uključujući taljene ledenjake u Jacobshavn zaljevu – potvrđuju ova promatranja.

article_content: A woman who spent a day and a half using drugs while a toddler lay dead in the closet of her home was sentenced Thursday to 22 years in prison. Laurie Cournoyer, 29, and her husband, Taylor, used methamphetamine, sleeping pills, and marijuana during an extended drug binge while responsible for several children—including RieLee Lovell, who died. Prosecutors allege they did not call 911 until 14 hours after discovering the child’s body. Cournoyer was sentenced to 10 years for possession of methamphetamine, five years for maintaining a drug premises, and 10 years (with eight suspended) for possessing drugs while incarcerated. She also received five years for failing to report the death of a child—a felony under a new South Dakota law modeled after 'Caylee’s Law'. RieLee Lovell, 2, was strangled to death on July 3, 2012, by her 11-year-old cousin while the Cournoyers were incapacitated by drugs. Authorities became aware of the death only after another child under their care showed neighbors the body hidden in a closet at their home in Warner, South Dakota, located in a Yankton Sioux tribal housing community. Cournoyer told the judge, 'It hurts my heart to know that I failed them—not only as a mother, but as a protector.' She added, 'I chose to put that needle in my vein. For the rest of my life, I must live with that choice.' She acknowledged creating an environment where harm occurred because she was high, and urged awareness of methamphetamine’s devastating impact on her community: 'Meth is hurting our people—our families, our community. Most importantly, our children.' Her husband, Taylor Cournoyer, pleaded guilty to drug-related charges and was sentenced to 13 years in November. An 11-year-old boy, whose identity remains confidential due to his juvenile status, has also been charged. His defense attorney described the incident as a 'perfect storm' involving a troubled child harming another child.

Također je osuđena na pet godina zbog neizvještavanja o smrti djeteta — kazneno djelo prema novom zakonu Južne Dakote koji je modeliran nakon 'Cayleejevog zakona'. article_content: Confidential personal data on hundreds of thousands of Britons is being sold by corrupt employees at Indian call centres, an undercover investigation by The Sunday Times has revealed. Credit card information, medical records, and financial details are being offered for as little as 2p to criminals and marketing firms. Two individuals posing as IT consultants met undercover reporters and claimed to possess 45 distinct datasets containing personal information on nearly 500,000 British citizens. The data included names, addresses, phone numbers, credit and debit card start and expiry dates, and the three-digit CVV security codes. Much of the information pertained to customers of major UK financial institutions, including HSBC, NatWest, Barclays, Halifax, and Lloyds TSB. One consultant, Naresh Singh, demonstrated the data during a meeting in a Gurgaon hotel room, stating he could identify the issuing bank simply by the card number. He confirmed the data was often less than 72 hours old and included newly issued cards. Additional sensitive information being traded included mortgage records, loan applications, insurance policies, mobile phone contracts, and Sky TV subscriptions. This data enables both fraudulent activity and highly targeted direct marketing. India’s call centre industry, valued at approximately £3.2 billion annually, employs around 330,000 people, many of whom handle outsourced services for British companies. While public backlash has led some firms — such as Santander, which owns Abbey — to discontinue outsourcing to India, data breaches remain underreported due to corporate fears of reputational damage. UK MP Richard Bacon, a member of the Public Accounts Select Committee, has urged the British government to investigate these allegations, stressing that responsibility extends beyond individual companies to national authorities. Indian officials acknowledge that efforts to combat corruption are hindered by a lack of reporting from private firms.

Informacije o kreditnim karticama, medicinske i finansijske podatke nude se za samo 2 penija kriminalcima i tržišnim firmama. Podaci su uključivali imena, adrese, brojeve telefona, datume početka i isteka kreditnih i debetnih kartica, kao i trocifreni CVV sigurnosni kod. Većina podataka se odnosila na klijente velikih britanskih finansijskih institucija, uključujući HSBC, NatWest, Barclays, Halifax i Lloyds TSB. Jedan savetnik, Naresh Singh, pokazao je podatke tokom sastanka u hotelu u Gurgau, rekavši da može da identifikuje banku izdavača samo na osnovu broja kartice. Ovi podaci omogućavaju i krađu identiteta i vrlo ciljano direktno marketinško delovanje. Indijska industrija call centara, vredna otprilike 3,2 milijarde funti godišnje, zapošljava oko 330.000 ljudi, mnogi od kojih rade na outsorcing usluga za britanske kompanije. Iako je javni protest doveo do toga da neke firme — kao što je Santander, vlasnik Abbey — prestanu sa outsorcingom u Indiju, povrede podataka ostaju nejavljene zbog straha kompanija od štete reputaciji. Britanski poslanik Richard Bacon, član Izbora za javne račune, pozvao je britansku vladu da istraži ove optužbe, naglašavajući da je odgovornost šira od samih kompanija i obuhvata i nacionalne autoritete. Indijski zvaničnici priznaju da su njihovi napori da se bore protiv korupcije ometaši nedostatkom prijava od privatnih firmi.

article_content: A British inventor has unveiled the Fuel3D scanner — a £650 handheld 3D device inspired by Star Trek’s tricorder. Capable of capturing high-resolution 3D models of anything from flower petals to human skin in seconds, the scanner sends data directly to a computer for processing. When paired with a 3D printer, it can recreate physical objects — from broken household parts to lifelike 3D portraits. Originally developed at Oxford University for medical imaging, the technology has been adapted for broader creative use. Its core innovation combines geometric and photometric stereo techniques to capture not just shape, but true color — something traditional stereoscopic cameras cannot do. 'The explosion of 3D printing and the growth of the gaming industry have driven demand for affordable, high-quality 3D scanning tools,' says Stuart Mead, head of Fuel3D Inc., which is funding development through Kickstarter. Roger Chang, CEO of 3D printing firm Pirate 3D, notes: 'The biggest barrier to home 3D printing isn’t the printer — it’s creating the digital models. Fuel3D could solve that.' Developer James Paterson adds: 'We’ve created a true point-and-shoot 3D scanner — no complex setup, no software training. And at this price, no one else offers this capability.' Experts believe this tool could spark a surge in consumer 3D modeling, bringing professional-grade scanning into homes and studios.

Kada se kombinuje s 3D tisakom, može reproducirati fizičke predmete — od slomljenih dijelova kod kuće do živopisnih 3D portreta. Izvorno razvijen na Oksfordskom univerzitetu za medicinsko slikanje, tehnologija je prilagođena za širu kreativnu upotrebu. Stručnjaci vjeruju da ova tehnologija može pokrenuti rast konzumerskog 3D modeliranja, donoseći profesionalni nivo skeniranja u kuće i studije.

article_content: Lewis Hamilton is fully immersed in his American dream—surrounded by rap stars, dating pop icon Nicole Scherzinger, and sporting a dazzling gold pendant featuring a Warhol-style portrait of his Mercedes car. The Formula 1 championship leader, who draws massive crowds in Austin, Texas, has openly considered building a future in the U.S., even raising a family there. 'I enjoy it here—it's pretty cool,' Hamilton said. 'New York is a great place to live. I was in Knoxville, Tennessee, recently. It’s beautiful by the lake. But there’s too much fast food.' He admits he hasn’t yet decided where to settle down, but the idea of starting a family and continuing his legacy is increasingly on his mind. At 29, Hamilton splits his time between his home in Monaco and Los Angeles, where he visits Scherzinger. He trains in Colorado’s Rocky Mountains and is deeply connected to the music scene—friends with rappers and exploring opportunities beyond racing. After parting ways with Simon Fuller’s XIX Management, he plans to choose a new representative by season’s end, with non-racing interests playing a major role. Hamilton’s distinctive style—diamond earrings, tattoos, a signature flat-brimmed cap, and now a bold gold pendant—sets him apart in the traditionally formal world of Formula 1. He designed the pendant himself and showcased it during a stop on ABC’s Today Show in New York, en route to the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, where he qualified second. He shared selfies with fans and celebrated alongside pole-sitter Nico Rosberg and third-place qualifier Valtteri Bottas at the Circuit of the Americas.

article_content: A North Sea oil worker, aged 43, returned home after a month-long shift to find his marriage in ruins — and his finances destroyed. His wife, 33, had spent his entire £75,000-a-year tax-free income, racked up £30,000 in loans under his name, and secretly traveled to London and Paris with other men. The breaking point came when he saw a Valentine’s Day post on Facebook: a photo of her in lingerie with the caption, 'Thank you for buying it.' He didn’t buy it. He’d never even seen the outfit. The message, he realized, was meant for someone else. Devastated and overwhelmed, he confronted her about the texts from Wonga and the unpaid mortgage. In the heat of the moment, things turned violent. He caused bruises to her face and body. She escaped through a window and hid. He smashed furniture and doors in anger. Though he admitted to causing bodily harm, a jury found him not guilty of rape. He claimed she initially consented to sex during a tearful conversation about ending their marriage, but stopped immediately when she said 'no.' She, however, testified that he ignored her protests and assaulted her. The man, described by coworkers as gentle and family-oriented, had never gone out drinking with colleagues to save every penny for his four children. Now, his home has been repossessed. He doesn’t know where his wife or kids are. His life, he says, has been shattered — not just by her betrayal, but by the accusation of rape, which he insists ruined everything. The court heard character references calling him a reliable, quiet man who prioritized his family above all else. Judge Phillip Wassall sentenced him to three months in jail, suspended for two years, noting the jury believed he didn’t instigate the violence.

Tačka preloma došla je kada je video post na Facebooku u dan Valentina: fotografiju nje u donjem rublju uz napomenu: 'Hvala što si mi to kupio.' On nije to kupio. Nikad nije ni video taj komad odeće. Poruka, shvatio je, bila je namijenjena nekom drugom. Ogorčen i preplavljen osjećajima, suočio se s njom o porukama od Wonga i neplaćenom hipotekom. U vreli trenutku, stvari su se pretvorile u nasilje. Povrijedio ju je i ostavio modrice na licu i tijelu. Ona je pobjegla kroz prozor i sakrila se. On je razbio namještaj i vrata u bijesu. Iako je priznao da je uzrokovao tjelesne ozljede, porota ga je oslobodila optužbe za silovanje. On je tvrdio da je ona prvo pristala na spolni odnos tijekom tužnog razgovora o završetku braka, ali je odmah prestao kad je rekla 'ne.' Ona je, međutim, svjedočila da je on ignorisao njezine proteste i napao je. Muškarac, koji su ga kolege opisali kao blag i obiteljski usmjeren, nikad nije išao na izlask u pivo s kolegama kako bi sačuvao svaku funtu za svoja četiri djeteta. Sada je njegov dom oduzet. Ne zna gdje su njegova žena ili djeca. Njegov život, kaže, uništen — ne samo zbog njezine izdaje, već i zbog optužbe za silovanje, koju on tvrdi da je sve uništila. Sud je čuo referencije od kolega koji su ga opisivali kao pouzdano, tiho osobe koje su obitelj stavile iznad svega. Sudac Philip Vassall osudio ga je na tri mjeseca zatvora, suspendirano na dvije godine, napominjući da je porota vjerovala da on nije započeo nasilje.

article_content: It was the book that captivated millions — but now, the publisher behind the global phenomenon Fifty Shades of Grey is facing serious legal allegations. Two women from Texas, Jennifer Pedroza and Christa Beebe, claim they were cheated out of their rightful share of the multimillion-dollar publishing rights to the bestselling trilogy. According to a lawsuit filed in Tarrant County Court, Texas, Pedroza and Beebe say they helped build The Writers Coffee Shop (TWCS), an online platform launched in 2009 that evolved into a virtual publishing venture. In 2011, TWCS released early editions of Fifty Shades of Grey, contributing to its initial momentum. They allege that Amanda Hayward, the Sydney-based co-founder of TWCS, secretly restructured the company in 2012 under the guise of tax optimization — without informing her partners — to ensure all proceeds from Random House’s deal flowed solely to her. Pedroza, who managed publicity, packed books, and organized events, says she received only a one-time $100,000 payment despite her substantial involvement. Beebe, who gave up a teaching job based on promises of long-term employment, was later terminated without compensation. The women’s attorney, Mike Farris, argues that TWCS was a true partnership under Texas law, and that Hayward never legally owned the publishing rights to the series. He contends she allegedly misrepresented ownership when negotiating with Random House and author E.L. James, potentially breaching fiduciary duties. Court documents also allege Hayward used portions of the earnings to purchase a lavish $5 million home in Dural, Sydney — complete with a pool, tennis court, and gym. The court has temporarily blocked Hayward from collecting further royalties. A hearing is scheduled for June 12 to consider a permanent injunction. The plaintiffs seek damages, a constructive trust on assets, and recognition of Pedroza’s 25% ownership stake in the profits. While the total revenue from the Fifty Shades franchise exceeds $100 million, the initial advance paid by Random House was approximately $3–5 million — a detail central to the legal dispute over profit distribution.

Dvije žene iz Teksasa, Jennifer Pedroza i Christa Beebe, tvrde da su prevarom isključene iz svog pravilnog udjela u višemilijunskim autorskim pravima na najprodavaniju trilogiju. Prema tužbi podnesenoj u Sudu okruga Tarrant, Teksas, Pedroza i Beebe kažu da su pomogle da se osnuje The Writers Coffee Shop (TWCS), online platforma osnovana 2009. godine koja se razvila u virtualno izdavačko preduzeće. U 2011. godini, TWCS je objavio ranije izdanja 'Fifty Shades of Grey', doprinoseći njegovom početnom uspjehu. One tvrde da je Amanda Hayward, ko-osnivačica TWCS-a iz Sidneya, tajno reorganizirala kompaniju 2012. godine pod izgovorom porezne optimizacije — bez obavještavanja svojih partnera — kako bi osigurala da svi prihodi od ugovora s Random House idu isključivo njoj. Pedroza, koja je upravljala javnim odnosima, pakovala knjige i organizirala događaje, kaže da je primila samo jednokratnu uplatu od 100.000 dolara, unatoč svojoj značajnoj ulozi. Beebe, koja je odbila posao učiteljice zahvaljujući obećanjima o dugotrajnom zapošljavanju, kasnije je otpuštena bez naknade. Advokat tužilaca, Mike Farris, tvrdi da je TWCS bio pravo partnerstvo prema zakonu Teksasa, te da Hayward nikada nije pravno vlasnik autorskih prava na serijal. On tvrdi da je ona navodno lažno predstavljala vlasništvo prilikom pregovora s Random House i autoricom E.L. James, što bi moglo predstavljati kršenje povjereničkih dužnosti. Dokumenti suda također navode da je Hayward koristila dio prihoda za kupnju luksuzne kuće od 5 miliona dolara u Duralu, Sidney — sa bazenom, teniskim terenom i gimnastičkom dvoranom. Sud je privremeno zabranio Hayward da prikuplja dodatne naknade. Članak za slušanje je zakazan za 12. juna, kada će se razmotriti trajna zabrana. Tužioci traže štetu, konstruktivno povjerenstvo nad imovinom i priznanje Pedrozinog udjela od 25% u dobiti. Iako je ukupni prihod iz franšize 'Fifty Shades' premašio 100 miliona dolara, početna napredna uplata od Random House iznosila je otprilike 3–5 miliona dolara — detalj koji je ključan za pravni spor o raspodjeli dobiti.

article_content: HONG KONG, China (CNN) — This week, the United Nations’ International Maritime Organization (IMO) convened in Hong Kong to draft new global rules for ship recycling. As delegates met at the city’s Convention and Exhibition Center, container ships gliding past them were destined for beaches over 1,500 miles away—in southeastern Bangladesh. Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan account for roughly 80% of the world’s end-of-life ships, according to the NGO Platform on Shipbreaking. Yet critics warn the proposed IMO convention fails to adequately address the dire health and environmental consequences of unregulated shipbreaking. Lee Adamson, IMO spokesperson, insists the new convention will be 'a tremendous step forward' in protecting workers and the environment by establishing standards where none existed. But Rizwana Hasan, lawyer and head of the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association, disagrees. Since 2003, she has fought to reform the industry through the courts, culminating in a landmark March ruling by Bangladesh’s High Court that forced tighter regulations—and earned her the prestigious Goldman Environmental Prize in April. Hasan’s central critique? The convention ignores 'pre-cleaning'—the removal of toxic substances like asbestos, lead, and PCBs before ships are beached. 'It’s the core issue,' she told CNN. 'Nothing is being said against beaching itself. Bangladesh’s beaches have become a natural disadvantage.' The shipbreaking industry is booming. With single-hull oil tankers banned from international waters by 2010 and global trade slowing, more vessels are being retired. Shipping companies often sell decommissioned ships to intermediaries who resell them to breakers—sometimes bypassing environmental rules by using 'flags of convenience' to evade the Basel Convention. In Chittagong, Bangladesh, laborers—including children—dismantle ships by hand, with no protective gear, exposed to lethal toxins. Accidents and deaths are common, though companies rarely disclose figures. 'I call it exploitation, not employment,' Hasan said. 'They get three meals a day, rarely pay, and always get sick.' Environmental damage is equally severe: heavy metals poison soil, oil leaks into oceans, asbestos fills the air, and mangrove forests—natural flood barriers—are cleared for yards. Fishing, once the region’s lifeline, has collapsed due to contaminated waters. Hasan isn’t calling for the industry to shut down. 'The workers have a right to speak,' she said. 'We need to transform it.' Since her legal victories, some companies now pay compensation for injuries—a small but meaningful shift. Though the Basel Convention provides a framework, it lacks binding authority over flag states. Adamson acknowledges this challenge: 'No convention can force a sovereign state to join if it doesn’t serve its interests.' For Hasan, the goal remains clear: 'Enough is enough. I don’t want to kill people and then pay compensation. I want an industry that doesn’t pollute—or kill.'
translated_content: HONG KONG, Kina (CNN) — Ovaj tjedan, Ujedinjene narodeva Međunarodna pomorska organizacija (IMO) je sastala u Hong Kongu kako bi razradila nove globalne standarde za reciklažu brodova. Dok su delegati sastali u Konvencionalnom i izložbenom centru grada, kontejnerski brodovi koji su proplivali pored njih bili su destinirani na plaže preko 1.500 milja daleko — u jugoistočnoj Bangladešu. Bangladeš, Indija i Pakistan čine otprilike 80% svjetskih završnih brodova, prema NGO Platformi za razbijanje brodova. Međutim, kritičari upozoravaju da predložena IMO konvencija ne pruža dovoljno rješenja za teške zdravstvene i ekološke posljedice neuređenog razbijanja brodova. Lee Adamson, govornik IMO-a, tvrdi da će nova konvencija biti 'veliki korak naprijed' u zaštiti radnika i okoline stvaranjem standarda gdje ih ranije nije bilo. Ali Rizwana Hasan, pravnica i predsjednica Bangladeške udruge za ekološko pravo, ne slaže se. Od 2003. boravi se za reformu industrije kroz sudove, što je rezultiralo važnom odlukom Višeg suda Bangladeša u ožujku kojom je prisiljeno jačanje propisa — i donijelo joj prestižnu Goldmanovu nagradu za okoliš u travnju. Njezina glavna kritika? Konvencija zanemaruje 'predčišćenje' — uklanjanje otrovnih tvari poput azbesta, olova i PCB-a prije nego što se brodovi izlože plažama. 'To je ključni problem,' rekla je Hasan CNN-u. 'Ništa se ne kaže protiv samog izlaganja na plažama. Bangladeške plaže postale su prirodna mana.' Industrija razbijanja brodova je u rastu. S obzirom da su jednokorišteni uljni tankeri zabranjeni na međunarodnim vodama do 2010., a globalna trgovina se usporila, više brodova se povlači iz službe. Pomorske kompanije često prodaju raspuštene brodove posrednicima koji ih dalje prodaju razbijačima — ponekad zaobiđući ekološka pravila korištenjem 'zastava pogodnosti' kako bi izbjegli Bazelsku konvenciju. U Čitatgonu, Bangladeš, radnici — uključujući djecu — razbijaju brodove rukom, bez zaštitne opreme, izloženi smrtonosnim otrovima. Nesreće i smrti su česte, iako kompanije rijetko objavljuju brojke. 'Zovem to eksploatacijom, a ne zapošljavanjem,' rekla je Hasan. 'Dobijaju tri obroka dnevno, rijetko plaću, ali uvijek dobiju bolesti.' Ekološka šteta je jednako ozbiljna: teški metali otrovaju tlo, ulje curi u oceane, azbest se oslobađa u zrak, a mangrove šume — prirodni zaštitni pojasevi protiv poplava — sječu se da bi se napravile radionice. Ribolov, koji je bio tradicionalni način života, uništen je zbog zagađene vode i malo ribe u obalnim vodama. Hasan ne traži zatvaranje industrije. 'Radnici imaju pravo da se izraze,' rekla je. 'Moramo je transformirati.' Od njezinih sudskih pobjeda, neke kompanije sada plaćaju naknadu za ozljede — mali, ali značajan pomak. Iako Bazelska konvencija pruža okvir, nema obvezujuću moć nad državama zastave. Adamson priznaje ovaj izazov: 'Nijedna konvencija ne može prisiliti suverenu državu da se pridruži ako to nije u njezinom interesu.' Za Hasana, cilj ostaje jasan: 'Dovoljno je. Ne želim da ljudi umru i onda platim naknadu. Želim industriju koja ne zagađuje — i ne ubija.'

article_content: Leading transport experts in the UK are urging government ministers to stop making sweeping economic promises about major infrastructure projects like HS2 and new road schemes unless they can provide credible evidence to back them up. In a strongly worded letter addressed to Transport Secretary Patrick McLoughlin, 32 leading academics alongside representatives from the Transport Planning Society and the Royal Town Planning Institute argued that reducing travel times on HS2 or expanding road tolling won’t necessarily deliver the economic gains claimed by officials. They emphasized that Britain’s cities are already saturated with traffic — gains from faster main roads are often negated by worsening congestion on local streets, where most daily journeys occur. The experts also criticized the Treasury for avoiding critical conversations around sustainable funding, particularly as vehicle excise duty revenue declines with the growing adoption of electric vehicles. Although they recognize public resistance, the group supports exploring alternative funding mechanisms such as pay-as-you-drive systems, stressing that a fair, long-term solution is urgently needed. Their stance mirrors a similar caution raised in a 2002 letter to then-Labour Transport Secretary Alistair Darling, underscoring persistent gaps in national transport policy.

U jasno napisanom pismu adresiranom ministru saobraćaja Patricku McLoughlinu, 32 vodeća akademika uz predstavnike Društva za planiranje saobraćaja i Kraljevskog instituta za urbanističko planiranje tvrde da smanjenje vremena putovanja na HS2 ili proširenje cestovnih naplata neće nužno donijeti ekonomske koristi koje tvrde vlasti. Naglašavaju da su britanske gradove već preopterećene saobraćajem — poboljšanja na glavnim cestama često se ponište zbog pojačane gužve na lokalnim ulicama, gdje se odvija većina svakodnevnih vožnji. Stručnjaci također kritikuju Ministarstvo finansija što izbjegava ključne rasprave o održivom finansiranju, posebno jer prihodi od poreza na vozila opadaju sa rastućom primjenom električnih vozila. Iako priznaju javnu otpornost, grupa podržava istraživanje alternativnih modela finansiranja poput sistema 'plati-po-kilometru', naglašavajući da je hitno potrebno pronaći pravedno, dugoročno rješenje. Njihov stav odražava sličnu opreznost iz 2002. godine kada je poslano pismo tadašnjem ministru saobraćaja Laboura Alistairu Darlingtonu, ukazujući na trajne praznine u nacionalnoj saobraćajnoj politici.

article_content: On Wednesday evening, Paris Jackson, 15, was visited by her mother Debbie Rowe, grandmother Katherine Jackson, and aunt La Toya Jackson at West Hills Medical Center in Los Angeles, where she is undergoing a 72-hour psychiatric hold following a suicide attempt. All three women appeared deeply affected, leaving the facility separately. According to a source familiar with her condition, Paris is now 'doing well,' smiling again, and eager to reunite with friends. Her siblings, Prince Michael, 16, and Blanket, 13, were not present. Paris has struggled with prolonged depression since her father, Michael Jackson, died in 2009. Sources say she has experienced emotional outbursts, self-harm, and intense feelings of loneliness, describing herself as missing her father deeply and feeling unloved. She recently reestablished contact with Debbie Rowe, who relinquished parental rights after her 1999 divorce from Michael. Katherine Jackson, her legal co-guardian, has supported this reconciliation as a step toward healing. The suicide attempt is believed to have followed an incident in which Paris was denied permission to attend a Marilyn Manson concert. Reports indicate she then self-harmed and contacted a suicide hotline. Paris has become a target of vicious online harassment, with Twitter users posting hateful messages including threats, slurs, and attacks on her late father’s legacy. She has publicly expressed a desire for emancipation from her family’s guardianship — a move that would grant her legal autonomy before turning 18. Katherine Jackson and Tito Jackson’s son currently share guardianship. Paris is also a plaintiff in Katherine Jackson’s ongoing lawsuit against AEG Live, alleging negligence in Michael Jackson’s death. Legal representatives have urged privacy for Paris during the trial. Active on social media, Paris shares candid moments — from makeup tutorials to quotes from Beatles songs — revealing her inner turmoil. One viral YouTube video, in which she jokes, 'I’m crazy,' was posted without her consent, prompting her to ask fans not to judge her for being 'weird.' In a message shared via TMZ, Marilyn Manson offered support, saying, 'I hope you feel better. You will be on my guest list anytime you want.' Conrad Murray, the doctor convicted of causing Michael Jackson’s death, also sent a message from prison — a gesture widely viewed as inappropriate and insensitive.

Sve tri žene izgledale su duboko zahvaćene i napustile objekt odvojeno. article_content: Steve Bruce sat with his tie loosened and exhaled deeply — no words were needed. His expression said it all: relief. After guiding Hull City to their first-ever qualification for European football in 110 years, he could not bear the thought of their dream collapsing after just seven days on the continent. With only ten minutes remaining, Hull were moments away from humiliation — until substitute Sone Aluko scored his first goal since September. 'You’re always nervous at 1-1 with 15 minutes to go,' Bruce admitted. 'All the hype, all the excitement — we nearly fell at the first hurdle. But we kept going, just like we always do, and we got through.' It hadn’t been easy. Just 90 seconds into the match, Tomas Malec stunned the sell-out crowd with a low, precise finish from 12 yards following a rapid Slovakian counterattack. Shane Long squandered three clear chances, and it wasn’t until the 27th minute that Ahmed Elmohamady headed home Robbie Brady’s cross to give Hull the lead. The second half threatened to fizzle into disappointment — until Bruce introduced Aluko and Tom Ince. At the 80th minute, Elmohamady raced down the right flank, crossed for Robert Snodgrass, whose header found Aluko unmarked — and the Nigerian winger smashed it home. 'I truly believe bringing those players off the bench won us the game,' Bruce said. 'Aluko and Ince brought fresh energy. I’m thrilled Aluko got the winner. He looked the fittest he’s been in seven years. He’s got incredible talent — let’s hope he stays fit. If he does, he’ll be vital for us.' Bruce reflected on the shaky start: 'We got off to a terrible beginning. That put everyone on edge for 25 minutes. We missed three or four golden opportunities — you start wondering, “Are we going to pull this off?” But we did. And I’m more proud for our fans than anything else. One supporter came up to me before kick-off and said, “I never thought I’d see this day.” That’s priceless.' Hull will find out their playoff opponent today. While Bruce expects improvement from a disjointed performance, he remains determined to strengthen the squad. 'I’ll always knock on the door for quality. The day I stop trying is the day I should quit,' he said. 'If there’s someone who can elevate us, I’ll chase them. Based on tonight? We might need one or two more to keep the dream of Inter Milan coming to Humberside alive.'

Nakon što je vodio Hull City do prve kvalifikacije za europsko takmičenje nakon 110 godina, nije mogao podnijeti misao da bi njihov san propao nakon samo sedam dana na evropskoj sceni. Sa samo deset minuta preostalo, Hull je bio na rubu ignominije — dok je zamjenski igrač Sone Aluko postigao svoj prvi gol od septembra. 'Uvijek se brineš kad je rezultat 1-1 sa petnaest minuta preostalo,' priznao je Bres. 'Sav haos, sav entuzijazam — skoro smo padli na prvom prepreci. Ali smo se držali, kao uvijek, i uspjeli.' Nije bilo lako. Samo 90 sekundi nakon početka utakmice, Tomas Malec je šokirao pun stadijon niskim, preciznim pogotkom sa 12 jardi nakon brzog slovačkog kontra napada. Šejn Long je propustio tri jasne prilike, a tek je na 27. minuti Ahmed Elmohamady glavom postigao gol iz centra Robbieja Bradija kako bi dao prednost Hullu. Druga polovica je prijetila da se pretvori u žalosan završetak — dok Bres nije uveo Aluka i Toma Inca. Na 80. minuti, Elmohamady je trčao uz desnu stranu, centrirao za Roberta Snodgrasa, čiji je zaglavio pronašao Aluka neoznačeno — i nigerijski krilo je udarilo s jakom silom. 'Zaista vjerujem da su nam zamjene donijele pobjedu,' rekao je Bres. 'Aluko i Ince su donijeli svježinu. Oduševljen sam što je Aluko postigao pobjednički gol. Izgledao je najbolje u posljednjih sedam godina. Ima ogroman talenat — nadamo se da će ostati zdrav. Ako bude, bit će ključan za nas.' Bres je razmislio o lošem početku: 'Otišli smo loše. To je stavilo sve na nervozu tijekom 25 minuta. Propustili smo tri ili četiri sjajne prilike — počneš se pitati, „Hoćemo li ovo uspjeti?“ Ali smo uspjeli. I ja sam ponosniji našim navijačima nego na bilo što drugo. Jedan navijač mi je došao prije utakmice i rekao: „Nikad nisam mislio da ću ikad vidjeti ovaj dan.“ To je neprocjenjivo.' Hull će danas saznati protivnika u play-off rundi. Iako Bres očekuje poboljšanje od neugodnog nastupa, on ostaje određen da pojača tim. 'Uvijek kučam na vrata za kvalitet. Dan kada prestanem tražiti, to je dan kada bih trebao odustati,' rekao je. 'Ako postoji netko tko može podići naš nivo, uvijek ću ga pratiti. Prema danasnjem nastupu? Možda nam treba još jedan ili dva da održimo san da Inter Milan dođe na Humberside.'

article_content: Lance Armstrong is due to appear in court next month after allegedly crashing into two parked cars and leaving the scene without reporting the incident. According to a police report, the crash occurred in late December in Aspen, Colorado. Armstrong and his girlfriend, Anna Hansen, departed the scene before officers arrived. Initially, Hansen told police she had been driving the couple home from an Aspen Art Museum party. She claimed that, due to icy conditions and excessive speed, she lost control and struck two parked cars. She said she spoke to the owners and offered to pay for damages. However, one officer interviewed a valet from the party, who stated that Armstrong had been the driver. Following this, Hansen revised her statement, admitting she was a passenger and that Armstrong had been driving. Hansen told police the decision for her to take blame was a 'joint decision' between her and Armstrong, made to avoid negative headlines. The charges have now been transferred to the 43-year-old former cyclist, who was stripped of his seven Tour de France titles and banned for life in 2012 after admitting to using performance-enhancing drugs. Armstrong is scheduled to appear in court on March 17.

article_content: A 71-year-old woman known locally as 'Britain's nastiest granny' has been issued an interim Anti-Social Behaviour Order (ASBO) after a 12-year campaign of harassment that left neighbors traumatized. Joan Nisbet, who currently serves a four-month prison sentence for breaking a prior court order, is set to be released on June 15. Upon her return, she will be legally barred from contacting, threatening, or disturbing her neighbors in Kenley, Surrey — including the Crowley family, who say she once sprayed weedkiller into a woman’s face and played deafening music for years. Croydon Council has gone further than usual, requesting a temporary closure of Nisbet’s home — a measure typically used for illegal drug operations — arguing that her conduct has made the neighborhood unsafe. Though the council has paused plans to evict her permanently, they insist that strict behavioral controls are vital once she returns home. The new ASBO prohibits her from shouting, swearing, playing loud music, banging on walls, or even appearing near the homes of those who reported her. It also forbids her from reaching out to witnesses who testified against her. The order remains provisional until August 14, when a full hearing will determine if it becomes permanent. Neighbors described living next to Nisbet as a daily nightmare. One resident said she endured 12 years of relentless abuse, including insults directed at children and psychological torment so extreme that a neighbor attempted suicide. At her September trial, Lorraine Crowley called her 'evil' and pleaded for long-term action. While the court previously imposed a suspended sentence, Nisbet’s continued violations prompted the council to escalate legal measures. Prosecutors emphasized that the previous restraining order failed to deter her, and the ASBO is now seen as the best tool to protect the community. No statement has been offered by Nisbet herself, who reportedly remained expressionless during the hearing.

Vijeće Croydon je otišlo dalje od običnog, zahtijevajući privremeno zatvaranje Nisbetine kuće — mjera koja se obično koristi za ilegalne droge — tvrdeći da je njeno ponašanje učinilo susjedstvo nebezbednim. article_content: Warring mobile operators in the UK could delay the launch of superfast 4G networks. Talks among providers aiming to roll out 4G services are currently at a critical juncture, insiders say. EE — the newly rebranded company formed from Orange and T-Mobile — plans to launch its 4G network on October 30th, using devices such as the Apple iPhone 5. CEO Olaf Swantee confirmed the date, but the rollout depends on access to radio spectrum currently used by air traffic control, analog television broadcasts, and legacy Olympic/Paralympic communications. EE and other operators are urgently requesting Ofcom to move up the 4G spectrum auction — originally slated for 2013 — and to accelerate the release of these frequencies. Without swift action, the entire 4G rollout could be delayed by more than a year. Other operators, including O2, argue that giving EE preferential access undermines fair competition. They warn they may pursue legal action, which could freeze the entire process until the auction concludes — likely no sooner than late 2013 or early 2014. A spokesperson for O2 emphasized that discussions aim to bring 4G to all UK consumers, not to block EE’s launch. The industry is exploring options to free up spectrum faster and establish MitCo, a new body designed to prevent signal interference and streamline planning for new mobile masts. Experts warn that delays would harm consumers and leave the UK lagging behind countries already enjoying 4G. Will Findlater, editor of gadget magazine Stuff, noted that slow rollout could push users to switch networks. London Mayor Boris Johnson supports EE’s initiative, but legal threats from rivals cast uncertainty over the timeline. A government-brokered 30-day standstill agreement temporarily halts litigation, but its expiry could trigger court battles. Analysts estimate the spectrum auction could generate £4 billion for the Treasury, raising the stakes. EE aims to cover 16 UK cities by Christmas and 98% of the population by 2014. Ofcom expects bidding to begin in early 2013, with consumer services launching mid-to-late 2013 — if delays are avoided.

CEO Olaf Swantee potvrdio je datum, ali je pokretanje ovisno o pristupu radio spektru koji se trenutno koristi za zračnu navigaciju, analogni televizijski prijenos i naslijeđeni spektar za Olimpijske i Paralimpijske igre. EE i drugi operateri hitno traže od Ofcom-a da pomakne natjecanje za 4G spektar — koje je prvobitno zakazano za 2013. godinu — i ubrza oslobađanje ovih frekvencija. Upozoravaju da mogu podnijeti tužbu, što bi moglo zaustaviti cijeli proces dok se ne održi natjecanje — vjerojatno najranije kasno 2013. ili rano 2014. godine. Predstavnik O2 naglasio je da razgovori imaju za cilj donijeti 4G svim korisnicima u Ujedinjenom Kraljevstvu, a ne da blokiraju pokretanje EE-a. Industrija istražuje opcije za brže oslobađanje spektra i osnivanje MitCo, novog tijela dizajniranog da spriječi smetnje signala i pojednostavi planiranje za nove mobilne tornjeve. Stručnjaci upozoravaju da bi odgoda štetila korisnicima i ostavila Ujedinjeno Kraljevstvo iza zemalja koje već imaju 4G. Will Findlater, urednik časopisa za elektroniku Stuff, primjetio je da bi sporiji uvođenje moglo potjerati korisnike da pređu na druge mreže. Stručnjaci procjenjuju da bi natjecanje za spektar moglo donijeti 4 milijarde funti blagajni, što povećava važnost vremena. EE planira obuhvatiti 16 britanskih gradova do Božića i 98% stanovništva do 2014. godine. article_content: Glenn Hoddle has stepped down from his role at Queens Park Rangers (QPR), following the unexpected resignation of manager Harry Redknapp on Tuesday. Hoddle, who served as part of Redknapp’s coaching staff, confirmed his departure from Loftus Road several hours after Redknapp’s announcement, citing the need for double knee surgery. 'I’m a bit shocked and surprised, to be honest,' Hoddle told ZapSportz. 'Football is undeniably results-driven, but I truly believed that with a few more games, Harry could have turned things around. The gap at the bottom is so narrow — just a couple of good results might have made all the difference. But that’s football.' Hoddle expressed gratitude to Redknapp for giving him the chance to return to coaching. 'I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. I wished him all the best, and I sincerely hope QPR can stay up. I’ve loved working with the players — and I hope I’ve helped them improve.' Sportsmail reports that Joe Jordan, Redknapp’s long-time assistant, is also leaving the club. In their absence, Les Ferdinand and Chris Ramsey will take temporary charge as QPR prepares to host Southampton in the Premier League this Saturday.
